For smaller models like Qwen3 8B and 14B, disabling the 3060s actually improved token generation speed (e.g., from 48 to 82 tokens/sec). For larger models, adjusting tensor split parameters improved performance: Qwen3 32B went from 13.0 to 15.6 tokens/sec, further rising to 16.4 with \"row\" split mode. Other models like Nemotron 49B (Q6) and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B (Q4) also saw modest gains from tuning. Interestingly, for Gemma3 27B and Mistral Small 24B, optimized tensor splits increased speed, but using the `sm` row mode slightly reduced it. Given these mixed results, what practical advice or heuristics have you found for configuring tensor splits and split modes in llama.cpp on heterogeneous multi-GPU rigs? Are there patterns in when \"row\" or other modes help or hurt performance? Any insights on balancing VRAM and compute across GPUs with different capabilities would be especially useful.
